title: Loving others part 2
scripture_text: “A new command I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
devotional:
How do we show love to others?

a. We need to take the initiative.

All these men were lounging around the table, then one of the disciples asked Jesus, ‘would you mind washing our feet?’

No that is not what happened.

Jesus acted because he saw a need, and an opportunity to show love.

Sometimes we complicate or over think things. If you have a thought about showing kindness to someone, just do it. You don’t need to over think it, or even pray about it, just do it. Don’t assume someone else will do it, or think, that is not my responsibility. We are all good at killing initiative. We find it so easy to rationalise deeds of kindness away.

Recently we had an experience when someone came to us at a gathering and insisted that they give us a gift of money. At the time we did not realise that a few hours later we would run out of oil, this person’s kindness helped us get oil. There are lots of ways to wash feet.’ You can visit, text, send a letter, make a phone call, provide food, pray with someone, take them for coffee, baby sit, invite them for a meal, give them a lift, take time to listen to them. And lots lots more...

b. Be spontaneous.

Look what John says ‘’The evening meal was in progress, and the devil had already prompted Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus. so he[Jesus] got up from the meal, took off his outer clothing, and wrapped a towel around his waist. After that, he poured water into a basin and began to wash his disciples’ feet, drying them with the towel that was wrapped around him.’’

There was no fan-fare, no big announcement, Jesus just stopped what he was doing, he stopped taking part in the meal so he could wash their feet.

When you feel that you should ‘wash someone feet,’ act as soon as you can, and sometimes that will require immediate action, where we will have to stop what we are doing. Sometimes our refusal to act immediately may rob us of an opportunity to show appropriate love.

c. Be sacrificial.

It was proper hospitality to offer your guests a basin of water for their feet. But guests were usually expected to wash their own feet. Washing the dirt off someone else’s feet was a task reserved for only the lowest ranking Gentile servants, and Jewish slaves were often exempt from this duty. In a household without slaves, everyone washed his or her own feet.

In washing the feet of his disciples Jesus was sacrificing his reputation.

It is okay to loose your reputation for the sake of showing selfless love to others. Sadly many people loose their reputation because of selfish sinfulness and in the process they hurt others.

d. The expression of love is more important than the success of love.

As you read through this passage you get the feeling that the disciples didn’t really get what Jesus did. In verse12 Jesus said, ‘Do you understand what I have done for you? We read about Peter’s difficulty in accepting what was happening and Judas walked away.

Loving others the way Jesus loves us is not a panacea, it is not a guarantee for success. That has to be okay.

There are two things we need to notice as we conclude.

1. Jesus has promised that ‘If we love one another as He has loved us, everyone will know we are His disciples.’

The radical ongoing expression of sacrificial foot washing love is the only way we have of getting the attention of the world outside. We don’t need more programmes, better advertisements, slicker services, but radical love for one another.

2. Jesus said in verse ‘Now that you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.’ Knowing, doing, blessed. The word used for blessed is the Greek word ‘Makarios.’

Writing about this word Ray Pritchard writes that makarios "doesn’t even apply to human emotions. It’s a statement of how God views people who live a certain way. The root idea of blessed is “approved by God.” preceptaustin.org.

I love this picture, Jesus is showing radical love of ‘feet washing’ to his disciples, and his father is in heaven standing clapping with great approval and delight. Have you ever watched your child on the stage or on the sports field, and the pride and joy you feel as they perform. When we adopt a ‘foot washing’ attitude to life so we can love others the way Jesus loves us we will be sustained by the approving applause of heaven, we will be blessed.

Questions you may want to consider.

1. Can you identify any insecurities that may be preventing you from showing the radical love of Jesus to others?

2. What does the act of ‘foot washing’ look like in your everyday life?
prayer: Father Help me to initiate love for others.
